COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLCON No. 59 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, learned counsel 
for the petitioner.
2. Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned C.S.C. for the 
respondents.
3. In pre-lunch session the S.S.P. Udham 
Singh Nagar, District Forest Officer, Udham 
Singh Nagar and District Mining Officer, 
Udham Singh Nagar were directed to form a 
committee to make a surprise visit to the site to 
verify whether any illegal mining activities are 
going on and then apprise to this Court today 
itself.
4. After post-lunch session Mr. P.C. Bisht, 
learned C.S.C. placed before this Court the 
report of S.S.P. Udham Singh Nagar dated 
23.04.2026 along with the pen drive which 
were also sent through whatsapp to the 
counsel for the petitioner. The pen drive and 
report are taken on record.
5. Put up this matter on 24.04.2026 as a first 
case before me keeping the matter as part 
heard.
6. Let fresh report be also furnished before 
this Court on 24.04.2026 at 10:30 am. The Court 
is not specifying the time for visit and 
inspection and this is for the authority to fix 
the time for inspection and how the surprise 
inspection is to be done.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
23.04.2026
Parul

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLCON No. 59 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, learned counsel 
for the petitioner.
2. Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned C.S.C. for the 
respondents.
3. Senior Superintendent of Police, Udham 
Singh Nagar, District Forest Officer, Udham 
Singh Nagar and District Mining Officer, 
Udham Singh Nagar joined the proceeding 
through V.C.
4. Two inspection reports in a pen-drive 
has been placed before this Court and this 
court perused the same and after perusing it 
reveals that regular illegal mining activities are 
going on in the area reference of which has 
been given in the order dated 23.05.2025 
passed in WPPIL No. 56 of 2025. I also perused 
the report of the officers from which it reveals 
that the officials physically inspect the spot, 
however, this Court is of the view that the 
officials are not aware how the inspection 
should be carried out. The Division Bench in 
another order dated 25.08.2025 passed in 
WPPIL No. 56 of 2025 observed as under:-
7. The Government shall also submit a 
report with regard to action to be taken to prevent the 
illegal smuggling of mineral across the border. The 
Government shall also submit an action plan for night￾time surveillance of sensitive areas and the border areas 
where it is alleged that illegal operators carry out 
mining during the night and transport the same before 
day break. In fact, in one case, a District Magistrate in 
one of the border areas had submitted that these illegal 
operators come fully armed with semi-automatic 
weapons, and that they pose a serious threat. If that be  the case, we wonder what the police department is up to.
8. The Secretary (Mining) shall personally 
look into this issue and submit an action plan to prevent 
such illegal mining.
9. This Court is of the opinion that it would 
be preferable if the department resorts to aerial 
surveillance by using drones during night-times. The 
department may also consider establishing a control 
room wherein the live images relayed by the drones can 
also be shared on real time basis with the local Police 
Station. The Government may also consider reinforcing 
the strength of the Police Stations and also ensure that 
the policemen in these sensitive areas are equally well 
armed to enforce the law and to defend themselves in the 
course of any engagement.”
5. On perusal of para 9 of the aforesaid 
order, the Division Bench opined that the 
department should prefer to resort aerial 
surveillance by using “Drones” during night￾times and to consider about establishing a 
control room. This order was passed on 
25.08.2025 and almost 11 months have been 
passed but there is no progress and illegal 
mining activities still going on. 
6. The District Mining Officer who joined 
the proceeding through V.C. submits that since 
last two to three years penalty has been 
imposed on the persons who are indulged in 
illegal mining activities. Such an excuse is not 
acceptable. Imposing penalty does not mean 
that illegal mining has been stopped. If the 
department is focusing only on imposing 
penalty that means they are not focusing on 
stopping the illegal mining activities.
7. D.F.O. also joined the proceeding 
through V.C. and submits that he himself 
visited the spot and it reveals that in large scale 
the mining activities are going on.
8. Let Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned Chief 
Standing Counsel may get further instructions 
why department is not using a drone 
surveillance once Division Bench of this Court 
has already observed in the order dated  25.08.2025 passed in WPPIL No. 56 of 2025. 
Learned C.S.C. shall also furnish the details of 
persons against whom penalty was imposed 
on the charge of illegal mining activity and 
how many times penalty were imposed 
because this Court is of the view that if a 
person who indulged in mining activities and 
penalized for more than five times it means he 
acquired his assets movable or immovable 
through proceeds which he achieve through 
illegal mining, therefore, such assets should be 
treated as proceeds of crime.
9. List this case on 12.05.2026.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
24.04.2026
Parul

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLCON No. 59 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, learned counsel
for the petitioners.
2. Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned C.S.C along with 
Mr. J.S. Bisht, learned Standing Counsel for the 
State.
3. Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned Chief Standing 
counsel, apprised to this Court that in the entire 
area regarding which the writ court passed an 
order, as on date no illegal mining activity is 
being carried out. If it is so, then the attempts 
made by the officials are really appreciable, 
however, the question is whether the illegal 
mining activities are completely stopped 
forever and in case those who were indulged in 
illegal mining activity and penalized for more 
than five times, and acquired assets then 
whether those assets are the proceeds of crime, 
and if it so then what action should be taken to 
such proceeds of crime. 
4. It has also been apprised that against 
various persons FIR has been lodged. Now, the 
question is if the FIR has been lodged, is it 
sufficient? If yes in what manner, the 
investigation is being carried out.
5. In the written instructions the references 
have been given about certain FIRs and 
therefore this Court wants to know in what 
manner the investigation is being conducted. 
6. Put up this case on 19.05.2026. 
7. The concerned investigating officers shall 
join the proceedings through V.C. 8. Mr. P.C. Bisht also apprised to this Court 
that against those license holders who were 
found to be indulged in illegal mining activity,
recommendation has been made for cancelling 
their license as well as to blacklist them so that 
in future they may not get any mining license. 
The exercise as done by the officials after taking 
cognizance in this contempt petition is really 
appreciable and this Court hope and trust that 
in future they will take strict action against 
those who were indulged in illegal mining 
activity. 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
 12.05.2026
Nahid

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CLCON No. 59 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Bhupesh Kandpal, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned C.S.C along with Mr. J.S. 
Bisht, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
3. On the previous date this Court took 
cognizance on certain FIRs lodged against the persons 
who are indulged in the illegal mining activity and 
the I.O. concerned was also asked to join proceeding 
through V.C. to apprise this Court in what manner, 
they are carrying out the investigation and in 
compliance thereof with the concerned I.O.s joined 
proceeding through V.C. and apprise the status of 
investigation but it appears that they should be given 
some guidelines or training how to carry out the 
investigation pertaining to the illegal mining activity.
4. Let the Secretary Mining may organize a camp 
for training to train these I.Os. since there should be 
some clarity in their mind what is illegal mining 
otherwise it is very impossible for them to carry out
the investigation.
5. By the next date Mr. P.C. Bisht, learned C.S.C. 
may also get the instructions from the other areas to 
find out whether any illegal mining activity is going 
on or not and if yes disclose the area.
6. Put up this case on 08.06.2026.
7. Registry is directed to supply the copy of this 
order to learned C.S.C for necessary compliance.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
 19.05.2026
